name: Stair climbing
pattern: Stepping gait up a flight of stairs, one step at a time: each leg lifts the body one riser.
setup: Stand at the bottom of the flight, tall, eyes two or three steps ahead.
Rest a hand lightly on the rail if there is one.

steps.text: Place the whole foot on the next step, toes near the riser, heel on the tread.
Push down through the middle of the foot and heel and straighten the front leg to rise.
Lift the back foot clearly over the edge and place it two steps up.

cues.cue: Stand tall, lean a little from the hips; look two or three steps ahead.
cues.why: A small forward lean shifts work to the hips and lowers the load on the knee.
A full foot gives a bigger base and stops the calf doing all the lifting; the foot cannot slip off the edge.

cues.cue: Push up through the front leg, not off the back toes.
cues.why: The knee and hip extensors of the leading leg lift the body in the pull-up phase.
A knee that falls in raises patellofemoral stress.

cues.cue: Steady pace, breathe in for two steps and out for two.
cues.why: 80-100 steps a minute keeps steady cardio work.

breathing: Rhythmic: in for two steps, out for two.

mistakes.name: Knee caves in
mistakes.looks: The knee drops inside the line from hip to foot while the foot is on the step.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knee over your second toe.
mistakes.why: Hip adduction and internal rotation load the kneecap unevenly; a little more forward lean reduced it.

mistakes.name: Only toes on the step
mistakes.looks: The ball of the foot sits on the edge and the heel hangs.
mistakes.fix: Put the whole foot on the step, toes near the next riser.
mistakes.why: Smaller base, the calf does the lifting, and the foot can slip.

mistakes.name: Head down, hunched
mistakes.looks: Folded at the trunk, eyes on the feet.
mistakes.fix: Chest up, look two or three steps ahead.
mistakes.why: Folding further hides the stairs ahead and closes the chest.

safety: Use the rail on steep or unfamiliar stairs.
Going down is mostly eccentric and loads the kneecap more: go slower and use the rail.

variants.change: Fast, one step at a time: MET 9.3 (17134).
Two steps at a time: hip 51° and knee 52° range against 30° and 41°; MET 7.5 (17136). Needs its own clip.
Stair machine: HealthKit stairClimbing; the stairs move, same cues; do not lean on the rails.
Going down: own clip and cues, slower, whole foot, rail.

motion.basis: Joint ranges from physiopedia-stairs (after McFadyen and Winter 1988) and protopapadaki2007; exact timing and the baked clip are ours (Body/anatomy/climb_za.py, 90 steps/min, 175 mm rise, 280 mm going).
